runtime.command_template: python -B tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <pinned-pinmame64.dll> --game <robo_a34|robo_a30> --rom-path <legal-ROM-root> --work-dir <fresh-state> --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/data-east/robo-a34-service-walk.json --boot-wait 2 --output <external-run>; robo_a30's ROM archive SHA-256 is 3dfe07399e5ea8ff98dd8cd9a18b5811044da1b6d4b9785ea509f0e103874aaa.

robo-a30.note: The builder required every Switch Test, Lamp Test and Coil Auto reading of robo_a34 to appear identically in this run, and the Coil Auto order to match; it did, so the frames are not repeated.

robo-a34.limitation: Each address carries two responses: the first Player 1/2 frame in its window whose text equals the curated name after folding 0/O and 5/S, and the Player 3/4 frame giving its wire code and address (Coil Auto: its bank code). Where several unfitted addresses print NONE in a row the display emits no new name frame, so the retained name frame is the one still shown when the window opened. A ROM name identifies the feature the ROM's own test assigns to the address; it does not prove the feature is fitted, its polarity or its location.

named_action_observations.label: Switch Test: host closes each matrix address and holds each flipper key; the ROM names it on Player 1/2
Lamp Test: each Start press steps one lamp; the ROM names the lit address on Player 1/2
Coil Auto: the ROM fires each output in turn and names it on Player 1/2
